title: Turnkey house or shell and core: which is better value
seo_title: Turnkey House vs Shell and Core: Which to Choose
description: Turnkey house or shell and core in Ukraine: the difference, what is included, a sample budget from $600/m² and from $1,100/m², pros and risks of each, and how to choose.
lead: Turnkey or shell and core is a question everyone building near Kyiv faces. The first gives you a house ready to live in; the second, a smaller starting budget and freedom with finishes. We compare both approaches, run a sample calculation and explain who each suits.
photo_alt: Facade of a single-storey house with a carport and lighting at sunset — House 150 project
body: h2
What shell and core means, and what turnkey means
p

A shell (in Ukraine people call it a box) is a house with the structure built: foundations, walls, floor slabs and roof, with windows and the front door installed. You cannot live in it yet — building services, finishes and furniture are still ahead. The exact scope differs between contractors, so it is always fixed in the estimate and the contract.
p

Turnkey is a house you can move into: the structure is built, building services are installed, interior finishes are done, sanitary ware, doors and lighting are fitted. Optionally, furniture, procurement and landscaping too. In other words, everything that separates construction from living in the house is done by one team.
ul
shell: foundations, walls, slabs, roof — then you organise the rest yourself
turnkey: structure, services, finishes — the house is ready to move into
both need a house design project
h2
How much each option costs
p

Our confirmed rates: building the shell from $600 per m², a turnkey house with finishes from $1,100 per m². The difference looks large, but it reflects the scope of work that a shell owner will have to carry out anyway — just separately and with other people.
p

Example for a 150 m² house: shell from 150 × $600 = $90,000, turnkey from 150 × $1,100 = $165,000. The difference covers building services, finishes and everything that makes the house habitable. The exact figure for your house comes from the estimate based on the design.
p

The right comparison is not the shell price against the turnkey price, but the full cost of the house up to move-in. If after the shell you hire separate contractors for services and finishes, the total is the sum of their estimates — and the risks at the interfaces between them are yours.

h2
When a shell makes sense
p

A shell makes sense when you have the resources and experience to manage the next stages yourself, or already have trusted contractors for services and finishes. It is also chosen when the budget comes in instalments: first make the house weathertight, then do the finishes later.
ul
you are ready to coordinate several contractors yourself
your budget is spread over time
you plan to finish the house in stages
you have your own designer and crew for interior works
p

The risks of this option lie at the interfaces. Services installed by another team must match the structure: openings for ventilation, embedded ducts for utilities, space for the electrical room and boiler room. If the services design was not ready before the shell was built, some decisions will have to be redone.
h2
When turnkey is better value
p

A turnkey house suits those who want a finished result with a predictable budget and one party in charge. You do not look for a contractor for every stage, coordinate dimensions and schedules between them or work out who is to blame if something goes wrong. It is also the practical choice if you live abroad and cannot supervise several contractors in person.
ul
one contract, one estimate, one schedule
services built into the structure from the start
a warranty on the full scope of works from one company
less of your time spent on coordination
p

Another advantage is coherence. When one team designs and builds the house, architecture, interior and services are aligned: light fittings are where the outlets were planned, furniture fits its niches, and stairs and doors match the drawings.

h2
Comparison: shell versus turnkey
ul
starting budget: shell — smaller; turnkey — larger but complete
your time: shell — a lot of coordination; turnkey — minimal
quality control: shell — each contractor has their own; turnkey — one standard
warranty: shell — in parts from different contractors; turnkey — on the full scope
risk of rework: shell — higher at the interfaces; turnkey — lower
p
There is also a middle option: order the shell and services from one team, and the finishes later. The key is to have the services design ready before construction starts.
h2
How to compare contractors' offers
p

A price per square metre is a handy benchmark, but comparing on that alone is risky. One company includes windows and an insulated roof in its shell, another only walls and slabs. So look not at the headline figure but at the scope of work in the estimate.
ul
which structures and materials are included: foundations, walls, slabs, roof
whether windows, the front door and facade insulation are included
whether embedded provisions for services are planned
what finishes the turnkey option includes
how the price is fixed and what happens if the design changes
what warranty is given and on what scope
p

If two offers are based on the same design with the same scope, they can be compared fairly. Without a design, comparing prices means comparing assumptions — and the difference will show up later as extra invoices.
h2
What to decide before you start
p

Whichever option you choose, construction begins with a design. Architecture, structure, utility networks and the position of the house on the plot must be settled before the first cubic metre of concrete. The design gives an accurate estimate and makes contractors' offers comparable. More on our [house design](/en/house-design) page.
ol
define the floor area, number of storeys and layout
check the plot and utility connections
commission the architectural and services designs
get estimates for both shell and turnkey
compare the full cost to move-in and choose

faq: How much does a house shell cost?
Building the shell starts from $600 per m². For a 150 m² house that is from $90,000. The exact amount comes from the estimate based on the design.
How much does a turnkey house cost?
From $1,100 per m² including finishes. For a 150 m² house that is from $165,000.
Which is better value — shell or turnkey?
A shell has a smaller starting budget, but services and finishes have to be organised separately. Turnkey gives the full cost upfront, one party in charge and a warranty on the full scope of works.
Can I start with a shell and order finishes later?
Yes. The key is to have the services design before construction starts, so all embedded provisions and openings are built into the structure.
